meta.face: A Gallo-Roman patrician of about eighty-five with a pale complexion and a LONG face with a broad, heavy LANTERN JAW — a high, lined forehead, a large, straight, high-bridged nose, small, heavy-lidded pale-grey eyes under sparse, straight white brows, deep lines running from the nose to the corners of a thin, wide, firm mouth; short white hair under the mitre, and a short white beard clipped close along the square jaw; his eyes lifted a little, in prayer.
meta.basis: No likeness survives. The book tells of a senator of Autun, widowed, bishop at fifty-seven for thirty-three years, so he is painted very old; its engraving shows him mitred with a short beard, praying before two angels. The lantern jaw and patrician bearing are our choice for a Roman senator and keep him apart from the other aged bishops (`hilary` trapezoid, `damasus` rectangular, `polycarp` heart-shaped).
